The money map

Your household as a living neural map — people, their accounts, and the hubs money flows through (selected date range, corrections applied). Click a hub to dive in: the camera glides closer and its merchants materialise — the small ones appear as you zoom deeper, so a “+15” badge means 15 more are waiting below the surface. Double-click an open hub to fold it away and glide back out. Shared merchants (two people both paying Netflix) show as one node linked to both. Click any node for its story — a card slides in from the corner with the numbers and a shortcut to the right section. Drag, scroll to zoom, drag the background to pan.

People, accounts & statements

Structure matches the money map: a household, then the people in it, then each person's accounts and statements. Add current, credit, savings or cash accounts; upload your bank's own CSV or Excel export under the right owner \u2014 the importer maps the columns, you check them, and you see the whole statement before it lands (duplicates are skipped). Set opening balances so cash and goals reconcile. Everything stays in this browser.

🏠 Household

Shown as the root node on the money map when you have people. Rename anytime — it does not change your bank data.

Everything on every screen is shown in this currency. Changing it reformats, it does not convert — your stored transactions keep the currency they were imported in. Set up conversion under Wealth → Currency & exchange rates.

Partners, co-owners, and businesses each get their own branch under the household — then attach accounts to them below or when uploading a statement.

Upload a statement

CSV, Excel, a PDF, or a photo from this device — choose the file, then Prepare & preview. Text files stay in this browser. A photo or a scanned PDF is read by Lithifyte’s vision model (5 hosted pages free, then Plus) after you acknowledge how a page image is handled. On a computer, Photograph with your phone shows a QR instead.

Between your own accounts

Money moving between household accounts — credit-card payments, top-ups, savings moves — is neither income nor spending, so matched pairs are excluded from every figure on this page (the savings side of a deposit transfer still counts toward your goals). High-confidence pairs are excluded automatically; confirm or reject anything below.

Auto-categorisation — rules already applied

Every merchant → category decision the bank feed's auto-categoriser has already made, with its own confidence score, biggest money first. Spot a wrong one? Hit Fix — it pre-fills a correction rule below, and your rules always beat the auto-categoriser. Statement name variants (store numbers, card refs, SEPA tails) are grouped under one merchant — a N names chip marks a group: click it to see or split the names, or add your own merge at the bottom of the card.

AI categoriser

Nothing is applied automatically — every suggestion you accept becomes an ordinary rule you can reorder or delete. Savings, rent and anything gambling-shaped are flagged for your judgement. Lithifyte AI (hosted) sees merchant names and your category list only — no amounts, no dates, no notes. A local model (Ollama, LM Studio) stays on this machine and may use richer context. Ollama: start with OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*. The hosted artifact blocks localhost — open the downloaded file for a local model.

Tick rows to move a batch at once — that moves exactly those transactions and nothing else. ＋ Rule on a row builds an auto-categorisation rule from its name instead, so future statements sort themselves; where a name has a varying part (a card reference like C123GB) a pattern is suggested for you.

Fix the categories

The bank's auto-categorisation gets things wrong. Add a rule here and every chart, KPI and projection on this page recomputes instantly. Rules apply top-to-bottom — the first match wins, and ▲▼ reorders them — and a rule can be limited to an exact amount or a € range (so “AMAZON over €100” can differ from small Amazon spends). The special category “Deposit savings” means “this money counts toward my goals”; anything else is an ordinary expense. If a big monthly transfer is actually rent, change its rule's category to Rent — your true savings rate shows immediately.

RuleMatchesRecategorise asOn

Pattern matching: * stands for exactly one character, % for any run of them. C***GB catches C123GB and C481GB but not C12GB; C%GB catches all three. Everything else is literal.

Rules apply first-match-wins and are saved in this browser. To make them permanent (or to have the whole analysis re-written around them), use “Copy re-assess prompt” and paste it to Claude or any AI assistant along with this file.

Categories & colours

Click a swatch to give any category its own colour — the category chart and the money map recolour instantly. Add new categories here to use them in rules; ↺ resets a colour, × removes a category you created.

The leak report

High-frequency, low-value spending — the money that disappears without a decision ever being made. Transaction counts tell the real story; figures reflect your category corrections and the selected date range.

Covering

Where the leaks happened

One strip per leak, a bar per month across the range above. A steady monthly habit and a one-off blowout need completely different responses, so each strip is flagged with which it is. Months far above the leak's own norm are marked ⚠ spike — measured against the median, so a single big month can't hide inside its own average.

Alerts & reminders

What's coming, before it lands: your own reminders (bills, renewals, one-offs) plus automatic warnings — likely upcoming bills predicted from your recurring history, and goals that have fallen behind pace. Everything is computed in this browser. Optional: email yourself a one-shot newsletter-style digest (client-composed — we never store the message body).

Email me a money digest

Budget — spending pace

Set monthly allowances and track whether the month is on pace — any day, not just month-end. Create budgets by category (existing spend groups) or by rule (bespoke merchant groups like “Lidl + Tesco + Aldi”). Scope each budget to the whole household or a single account. Regular bills count from day 1 so early rent never false-alarms. Prefer Excel? Switch to the dark-header spreadsheet layout, or export a template and re-import.

Forecast & recurring costs

Similar amounts in 3+ of the last 4 months are treated as monthly; quarterly, 6-monthly and yearly rhythms (insurance renewals, motor tax) are detected across your full history and spread into the forecast. Fine-tune it: set when each one ends (car finance ends Jan 2028…), add items your statements can't see yet, and adjust the safety buffer — the cautious path holds back a share of your historical spending swings, and every goal verdict above uses it. Decembers get your historical uplift automatically.

Mortgage readiness

What a mortgage underwriter looks for in your last 6 months of statements — computed live from your data, not opinion. These checks (a visible savings pattern, no missed payments, clear categorisation, credit commitments in proportion) are what lenders ask about almost everywhere, though the exact thresholds and paperwork are your lender's. Green means application-grade; fix the ambers before you apply.

Beyond the deposit — the wealth engine

The machine you've built shouldn't idle once the deposit is done. Free money you can claim, what your pot earns while it waits, the pension lever (the best guaranteed return available to a 40% taxpayer), and where the surplus flows after every goal is funded. Figures are estimates from your data — verify current rules before acting.

Financial pulse

One dial over the whole household — seven measures across the Spend / Save / Borrow / Plan pillars, each scored against absolute benchmarks (never your own average, so a bad normal can't score as fine) and traceable to the exact numbers behind it. Flow measures follow the window you pick; balance measures (liquidity, long-term, debt, budgets) are as of today. Measures without data are left out and say why — the dial never pretends.

Window

Net worth

Every layer counted once: reconciled cash from your accounts, goal pots that live in accounts this file doesn't track, priced investments, and anything you add below — property, vehicles, a pension valuation — minus tracked debts and credit-card balances. Each manual value carries its as-of date and goes amber as it ages instead of silently pretending to be current; possible double counts are flagged, never guessed away.

Loans & debt

Track any mortgage, loan or card balance — even ones whose payments never appear in your statements. Enter the payment or an end date; exact amortisation derives the rest: payoff date, interest remaining, and the month the freed payment flows back into your forecast surplus. Commitments feed the mortgage-readiness capacity check. If the repayments are already in your statements, pick the merchant so the forecast ends them on time instead of double-counting.

the guided route checks as you go — it will tell you if a payment can never clear the balance

Currency & exchange rates

Rates for converting between currencies. Nothing about your money is sent anywhere — a refresh asks a public ECB rate feed for a plain list of rates, the same request any visitor to that site makes, and it carries no account, balance or transaction data. It is off until you press it, and typing rates by hand always works instead.

Rates against —

Investments & crypto

Your positions — shares, ETFs, funds, crypto, pension — priced from a quotes book you control. Quotes never leave this file: type them in (always works), hit ↻ for crypto (fetched keylessly from CoinGecko when this page is opened as a local file; the hosted artifact blocks external requests, so there it stays manual), or 📥 import a quotes-….json written by the feeder CLI (node feeder.mjs prices AAPL VWCE=VWCE.DE — keyless Yahoo quotes, converted from the file's currency into yours using the rates under Currency). If you enter your own tax rates under Your tax assumptions, each row also shows what tax that gain would attract on your figures. Lithifyte ships no tax rates and gives no tax advice.

Idle money

Your tax assumptions

Lithifyte does not know your tax rules and does not give tax advice. Tax differs by country and by person and changes most years, so this app ships no rates at all. Enter the ones that apply to you and the calculators below will do the arithmetic on your figures. Leave a field blank and anything that depends on it stays hidden. Check the current rules with your own tax authority or an adviser — these are your assumptions, not our advice.

Pension leverage

Notes & context

What the numbers cannot tell anyone: plans, circumstances, intentions. “Ben's hours drop every January.” “This is the joint account the house runs from.” “The savings are for a wedding in 2028, not a car.” Link a note to the people and accounts it concerns and it appears on their money-map nodes — and when you connect a local AI, this context goes with the numbers, so its advice is about your situation rather than a generic spreadsheet. Everything stays in this browser like the rest of your data.

Filter

Notes travel in your backup. Copy re-assess prompt and a local categoriser can include them; the hosted co-pilot does not get them wholesale — it asks for a scoped note if it needs one.

Updates

This copy is self-hosted, so nothing updates it but you. Lithifyte can check whether a newer version has been published and tell you — it asks GitHub, never us, so we do not learn that you exist, what version you run, or that you ran it today. Off until you turn it on, and it checks at most once a week.

Your account

Not signed in on this copy — self-hosted and downloaded files never phone home.

Google Drive

Back up an encrypted snapshot to a private app folder only this app can see, or pick a statement you already saved in Drive. We never ask to read your whole Drive.

Cloud vault (Plus)

Store one encrypted backup on Lithifyte’s host so a new browser can restore it. We receive the same ciphertext envelope as a local encrypted export — not the passphrase, not the ledger. Self-hosted copies never use this.

AI & what left this device

The ledger never lives on our servers. With consent, Lithifyte AI can read every panel and make reversible edits (budgets, goals, rules, notes). Imported statement amounts are never changed. Commands-only and a local model send nothing. Hosted intelligence, the encrypted vault and maintained bank-import presets are Plus; the Engine stays free forever, and export is never gated.

Data integrity
    Self-test running…

      Backup & restore

      Everything you configure — rules, goals, people, uploaded statements, recurring fine-tunes, colours — lives only in this browser. Export it to a file you keep; import it on any device (or after clearing browser data) to restore everything. Downloaded page + your backup file = fully self-hosted.

      Passphrase

      With a passphrase set, exports are AES-encrypted (same passphrase needed to import) and “Lock” keeps every store encrypted at rest in this browser — you'll be asked for the passphrase whenever the page opens. There is no recovery from a forgotten passphrase; keep an unencrypted backup somewhere safe if unsure.

      Pre-update snapshots

      When an update needs to change how your data is stored, this page copies every store into a restore slot first. If an update ever misreads your data, roll back here — then export a backup before trying the update again. Snapshots live in this browser only; the newest 3 are kept.

      checking…

      Your data is held at its restored version, so this build is not writing to it. Export a backup first; then lift the hold to let the update run again.

      Danger zone

      Erases everything this page stores in this browser — uploaded statements, rules, goals, people & accounts, budgets, notes, colours and settings — and returns it to a blank slate. Export a backup first; there is no undo.

      How to update with new transactions (for you, or any AI assistant)

      This page is self-contained: transactions, rules, goals, people, accounts, recurring fine-tuning and simulator levers live in a single JSON block (<script id="finance-data">), and every number is derived from it in the browser. Statements you upload live in this browser's storage — attach your backup file (Export everything, above) or the original CSVs when asking an AI to update the file. Say:

      Here is my dashboard HTML and my transactions CSVs (same columns as before). Follow the "FOR AI ASSISTANTS" comment at the top of the HTML: map the CSV rows into the "transactions" array (tagging each row with its accountId), keep/merge my "rules", "goals", "users", "accounts", "categories" and "recurring" arrays, and re-assess — goal verdicts, forecast, leaks, and rewrite the static advice cards if the picture has changed.

      To bake in everything you configured here (rules, categories, goals, people, recurring end-dates), use the “Copy re-assess prompt” button in the rules section — it includes all of it automatically.

      Notes on the data: Apr 2024 shows near-zero income because that month's wages landed in May (double payment). “Rent” in the raw data is irregular (two lump payments of €3,000/€2,500 to the same payee) — worth confirming how housing is actually paid, since a lender will ask the same question. Forecasts assume detected recurring items continue until the end date you set. Scheme details (Help to Buy, First Home Scheme, deposit rates) change — verify current terms before relying on them.
